gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.start.body:
# Plant your beacon
- Right-click a beacon item on the ground, read the confirmation, then plant it. There is one shared beacon per world, in the Overworld.
- Planting starts a short introductory raid at once. Win it to earn your Weapon Platform.
- Later raids wait seven ACTIVE Minecraft days. Nobody online? The timer pauses.
# Use it
- Right-click the beacon for Overview, Upgrades, Raid break and Settings. No commands needed.
- The Beacon Recovery Shovel opens the same controls from a distance, and shows beacon status while you hold it.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.start.detail:
- The introductory raid is fixed at tier 0.
- Raids that follow come faster as your reward tier improves, down to one every two active days.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.start.detail.pa: - Lost this book or the recovery shovel? Their cheap recipes are in JEI. The starter flintlock fires one shot and reloads slowly; ammo you spend stays spent.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.start.detail.st: - Lost this book or the recovery shovel? Both have ordinary crafting-table recipes, and JEI is optional. New players start with a weapon and matching ammunition.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.zone.body:
# The protected zone
- A moving cyan grid marks every protected block, including the ceiling and floor. Switch it on or off in Settings.
- The first footprint is 17 x 17 blocks: 8 blocks each way from the beacon.
- Three Core upgrades give Mk-2, Mk-3 and Mk-4 with radii 12, 18 and 24. Mk-4 needs a clear 3 x 3 footprint, two blocks tall.
- Vertical upgrades raise the height separately, up to 16 below and 48 above, without changing HP or the model.
# Build to score
- Newly placed building blocks all earn equal credit. Palette, details, lighting, furnishings and usable rooms earn bonuses.
- Natural terrain earns no bulk credit, and expensive ore blocks earn nothing extra.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.zone.detail:
- The cyan lines sit on the OUTER faces of the included blocks. One-block ticks help you count, and corners count too.
- A separate red outline in Settings shows the part of the beacon that enemies can damage. It starts three blocks below and eight above.
- Existing crafted blocks are recognized. Occupied, covered rooms also credit raw stone and dirt.
- Stations inside the zone add score. Only the highest Age of each of the four station types counts: 40 / 90 / 180 / 300 / 450 for Ages 1 to 5.
- Rewards & tiers previews the exact shared payouts, including wave iron and hard-raid bonuses.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.zone.detail.pac: - Build Create machines, turrets and Universal Platforms inside the zone. Factories and higher station Ages boost your score.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.zone.detail.sta: - Build turrets and Universal Platforms inside the zone. Higher station Ages boost your score.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.raids.body:
# Raids
- Ambient hostile mobs can attack an exposed beacon. They need line of sight and must be within 24 blocks, so solid cover hides it.
- Raid attackers always know where it is and can breach doors or walls. Build walls and defenses, and keep turrets stocked.
- Kill every attacker to win. Survivors glow after one minute; Reconnaissance makes them glow at once.
- Three defender deaths nearby cost the beacon health.
- Every third started raid is a hard raid: 25%% more attackers and a boss in the final wave.
# After the fight
- Victory restores tracked damage in the zone. Spent ammo, fuel and durability stay spent; a defeat leaves the damage behind.
- The beacon is the reward chest: press Reward chest in Overview and its 54 slots open. Collect again to refill it; overflow stays queued at the beacon. If the beacon is destroyed its contents spill out.
# Special raids
- From the fourth raid on, half of all raids are special (boss raids included): Air Raid (flyers that ignore walls), Paratroopers (heavy mobs on red parachutes), Siege (creepers breach, shooters follow) or They Are Thousands (only basic zombies, in swarms).
- The next raid's kind is announced when a raid ends and shown in Overview. A won special raid adds Ardent Energy to the reward.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.raids.body.pack: - The hard-raid boss is a modded boss with a red boss bar. Defeating it gives 50%% more completion resources plus bonus medical kits and grenades.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.raids.body.stan: - Without optional boss mods the boss is a vanilla Ravager. Defeating it gives 50%% bonus completion materials.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.raids.detail:
- Ordinary enemies have bounded health and no armor. Specialists have light armor, and marked heavies are uncommon.
- Special Forces begin at reward tier 4. Solo tiers 4 to 6 send one soldier per wave; heavies start at tier 7. When warned, get behind sandbags for a shootout.
- Downed Special Forces count as defeated, and their bodies stay lootable for up to ten active minutes.
- Extra nearby Survival or Adventure defenders raise reinforcement counts by 65%% each, not enemy health. The count locks at each wave and shows in Overview. Alive-enemy limits are 24 solo and 48 in co-op. Spectators, Creative players and distant players do not count.
- Veteran victories add at most 30%% reinforcements, with no hidden health growth. Boss health adds 45%% per extra defender, up to four.
- Defeats still count toward the three-raid cadence. Scheduled raids arrive at night.
- The reward chest needs two adjacent ground-level blocks clear with headroom, at least three blocks from the beacon, inside the zone. Create the first one between raids. Its 54 slots keep supplies out of your inventory.
- Higher reward levels shorten the next interval: 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, then 2 days.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.raids.detail.st: - Standalone rewards use vanilla resources, Ammo Coins and healing potions. Installed tactical consumables can also appear.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.control.body:
# Take a break
- Raid break buys five ACTIVE days before the normal countdown resumes. Each purchase costs more, and purchases stack for long expeditions.
- Offline time does not count toward a break.
# Choose the fight
- Lower level / Raise level sets a raid level cap from 0 to 10. The cap limits both enemies and payouts, including the purchased bonus. Your building score and upgrades stay intact.
- Start raid now begins at the displayed level without waiting for night, and ends any purchased break. Every third started raid still has a boss.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.control.body.pa: - Break price: brass, precision mechanisms and gold.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.control.body.st: - Break price: copper, diamonds and gold.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.control.detail:
- Purchases add up to three bonus tiers within your chosen cap.
- The next started raid uses the bonus and resets the purchase price.
- Starting a raid saves a snapshot of the base first. Ambient enemies stay active during a break.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.upgrades.body:
# Branches
- Core: larger zone and more HP (Mk-1 to Mk-4).
- Logistics: five levels add five reward tiers. Building adds up to five more, for tier 10 at most. Better tiers shorten raid intervals to two days.
- Defense: 15 / 30 / 45 / 60%% less beacon damage.
- Restoration: faster rebuilding and 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 25%% maximum-HP healing after victory.
- Vertical: more zone height, no HP or model change.
- Reconnaissance: attackers glow immediately.
# Buying
- Upgrade near the beacon between raids. Each card shows the material you hold; press Buy when you have enough.
- Creative mode purchases and upgrades are free.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.upgrades.body.p:
# Making components
- JEI shows the Create recipes for each upgrade component. Manufacture enough, carry them, then buy. Hover a material icon: {jei}
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.upgrades.body.s:
# Making components
- Craft reinforced plating, logistics modules, resonance coils and restoration matrices from vanilla materials at a crafting table. JEI is optional. Hover a material icon: {jei}
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.repair.body:
# Repair
- A disabled beacon needs Overview > Repair. Eight reinforced plating restore 250 HP and restart the timer.
# Pack up
- To stop the campaign, hold the Beacon Recovery Shovel near the beacon and use it, or choose Settings > Remove. Read the confirmation.
- Removal returns one beacon and resets ALL upgrades, progress and unclaimed rewards. Your base is kept.
- Repairs never refund spent ammo or fuel.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.repair.body.pac: - Park and disassemble moving Create contraptions before raids.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.stations.body:
# Four stations
- Weapon Platform: the gun catalogue and the Workshop. Win the introductory raid to claim it.
- Ammo and Attachment tables show only parts that fit the gun in your hand. Hold the gun and press [{interact}] while looking at the table, or right-click it with the gun.
- Armor Platform: helmets, vests, leg protection, boots, pouches, plates and vision gear. Open it empty-handed.
- Food, medical kits, grenades, tools and gear materials are in the Weapon Platform's Supplies category.
# Ages
- Each station upgrades on its own through five Ages: Frontier, World Wars, Modern, Advanced, Exotic.
- Choose Workshop at the Weapon Platform to buy tables and to upgrade placed tables within 8 blocks.
- Ammo Coins come only from completing raids. At the Ammo table, Buy with coins pays for the shown batch instead of materials.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.stations.body.p: - Modern and later Ages need a team visit to the Nether and the Create precision parts.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.stations.body.s: - Modern and later table Ages need your team to visit the Nether.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.stations.detail:
- Benches are two blocks wide and two tall, one deep, and turn to face you. Either half opens the same menu. Mining either half returns one station and keeps its Age; raid repairs do too.
- The Ammo table lists reusable EMPTY magazines as well as loose rounds. Use the filter to switch between loose ammunition and compatible magazines. Craft an empty magazine, then fill it with the magazine addon and your loose rounds. Coins can buy empty magazines but never include free rounds.
- Expanded magazines need a matching extension on your gun and a later Age. The browser counts items still locked behind later Ages.
- Use the coloured Age filter for weapon eras. Historical identity matters: a modern pistol stays a Modern unlock. Gauss and cyberpunk weapons are Exotic.
- Compatibility and Age locks still apply in Survival. Coin cost scales with Age and the strongest compatible gun damage, including pellets and explosives.

- Create Armory, Turrets and Supplies have separate category buttons. Supplies follow shared Create research instead of Ages: simple field gear starts unlocked, medical kits and grenades need Workshop research, advanced supplies need Precision research.
- Operate a press and mixer for Workshop, a deployer and a precision mechanism for Precision, and a steam engine for heavy Steam weapons. Turrets need Precision production and factory materials.
- Near-future MS-Mobius weapons need later factory Ages; Helldivers weapons require Exotic. Shared milestones also unlock matching Create Armory components.

- Weapon Platform uses the installed TaCZ gun, ammo and attachment indexes, even for guns without a native crafting recipe. Gunsmith menus are redirected to the platforms.
- Unknown firearms get a conservative Age and vanilla costs. Known historical guns keep their era. Automatic prices are a starting balance; admins can override both in config/arsenal-beacon-standalone.json, then restart.
- If Arsenal Displays is installed, its vanilla recipes defer to the Supplies category while the beacon is present.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.energy.body:
# Ardent Energy
- Hostile mobs rarely drop Ardent Energy: about one kill in fifteen (one in twelve in the standalone edition). A boss always drops one, and every won raid pays a guaranteed amount, more at higher reward tiers. It is a currency, not an ingredient.
- Spend it on flares and the cannon at your Support Platform, and at the Exchange Shop. In the standalone edition it also pays for upgrades.
# Exchange Shop
- Place an Exchange Shop inside your beacon zone (the weapon table's Workshop tab sells one). It has two tabs: Sell, where you hand in materials for Ardent Energy, and Buy, where Ardent Energy buys supplies at a higher price.
- A factory can sell its surplus; a hunter without a factory can buy parts. Buying always costs more than selling.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.energy.detail:
- Base drop chance 6.67%% (8.7%% standalone), +1%% per Looting level. Raid attackers count too. Tune it in config/arsenal-beacon-common.toml.
- Offers are plain text in config/arsenal-beacon-exchange.txt, in a [sell] and a [buy] section: 'minecraft:diamond = 6' is one diamond for 6 energy, 'minecraft:arrow x16 = 3' is sixteen arrows. The pack lists Create parts and the standalone edition rare vanilla materials.
- The shop reads its file every time it opens, so edits apply without a restart.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.support.body:
# Your support base
- Every player builds their own Support Platform and Support Cannon. Get the platform at the Weapon Platform's Workshop tab (or craft it), place it inside your Defense Beacon zone with the block in front of it clear, then buy the cannon at the platform.
- The platform and the cannon can go anywhere inside the zone, as far apart as you like, so build your base around them. The cannon has a plate with its owner's name; the platform carries a little sign on top. The two blocks in front of a platform (two tall) are a no-build zone, "KEEP RETURN ZONE CLEAR", so a Return Flare always has somewhere to put you; without a safe spot the flare is not used.
- Support gear stops working while the beacon is gone. Move it for free by right-clicking it with the Beacon Recovery Shovel; a platform keeps its Mk level and contents.
# Flares
- Every flare goes through your cannon: it turns toward the flare with a grinding of gears, and only when it has settled does it fire. That turn time comes first, and the flare's own delay only starts after the shot.
- Fill the supply grid, then throw a Support Flare. When the cannon has fired, a chest with everything in the grid arrives: parachuting in outdoors, or appearing at your feet underground. The grid is emptied.
- Return Flare: throw it, then step into the purple portal that opens where it landed to arrive at your platform.
- Fire Support Flare: throw it at enemies. A red box marks the area and your chosen shells land exactly on the flare, six of them by default. Throw a second one while a barrage is running and you are told "Barrage in process": it waits for the cannon.
- Throwing costs nothing; you pay Ardent Energy when you buy flares and the cannon at the platform. If something is missing you keep the flare and get a message.
- If you are far from your cannon, chat tells you "Cannon preparing" when it starts to turn and "You heard cannon fire roaring" when it shoots.
# Your cannon
- Click your cannon to choose your fire support and to buy upgrades with Ardent Energy. The choice is yours alone: a flare somebody else hands you still calls YOUR choice, and everyone is told what you called. Hold a Fire Support Flare and the chosen support is shown above your hotbar.
- Explosion Barrage, Arrow Cluster Bomb (2 more volleys), Narukami's Favor (lightning on every hostile mob, 1 fewer volley), Bunker Buster (one huge bomb that digs out everything in its box), Healing Barrage (heals players) and Curse of Debilitation (the worst debuffs on hostile mobs).
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.support.detail:
- Prices at the platform: Support Flare 3 energy, Return Flare 2, Fire Support Flare 6, Support Cannon 12. The Exchange Shop and the Support Platform are also sold in the Weapon Platform's Workshop tab for iron, copper, redstone and glass.
- Supplies arrive 12 seconds after the cannon fires for a flare that landed outdoors, or 7 seconds underground. Chat counts the seconds down. The time the cannon spends turning comes on top.
- The cannon is heavy: it spins up and brakes slowly, so a flare behind it takes longer to answer. It can only work on one call at a time.
- Fire Support lasts 12 seconds (6 shells). Each shell deals 25 damage to hostile mobs touching the red box (within 4 blocks of the flare) and never hurts players or breaks blocks.
- The Bunker Buster is the exception: its box reaches 8 blocks down as well as up and sideways, every block inside it is dug out (the Defense Beacon, base blocks and super hard blocks such as obsidian, crying obsidian and bedrock are spared), and it hurts every player inside for half their maximum health, whatever armor they wear. If its box touches your beacon zone the flare is handed back.
- The portal stays open for 30 seconds and only its owner can use it. It works from any dimension.
- Parcels disappear after 30 minutes and drop what is left inside.
- Upgrades Mk-2, Mk-3 and Mk-4 cost 16, 32 and 64 reinforced plating and grow the grid to 4 x 4, 5 x 5 and 6 x 6.
- Only the owner can open their platform or cannon.
- Each Area of effect level widens the area by 1.5 blocks each way.
- Each volley level adds 2 shells and each damage level adds 25 percent. Rate of fire cuts the gap between shells from 40 ticks to 33, 26 and 20.
- Without Quantum tunneling a fire support flare that lands below ground is handed back. Supply and return flares are not affected.
- Dimensional link lets fire support flares work in the Nether, the End and other dimensions (the cannon still needs your base to stand). Supply and return flares are not affected.
- The Lasting portal stays open for 5 minutes and works twice: once home, once back to where you threw it.
- The Healing aura circles a supply flare (6 blocks) and ends 30 seconds after the parcel is emptied.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.reference.body: ~ Exact numbers and extra rules from every other page, gathered in one place.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.coop.body:
# Together
- All players share one beacon, the raid level cap and the reward chest.
- The red BEACON IS BEING ATTACKED warning reaches every player, in any dimension, without holding a tool.
- Settings can switch the sky beam and the red damage outline off. The recovery shovel panel hides when you put it away.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.coop.body.pack:
# Pack co-op
- Invite your friend through Essential. Join one FTB Team to share quests. Use the same pack version.
# Pack keys
- {reload}: reload
- {emotes}: emote wheel
- {shaders}: shader reload
- {backpack}: backpack
- {quests}: quests
- {map}: world map
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.coop.body.stand:
# Standalone co-op
- Install the same standalone beacon and TaCZ builds on every player and on the server. Gun Guide is client-only and optional.
- This release does not remap other mods' keys or mute their chat. Change keys in the normal Minecraft Controls screen.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.coop.detail.sta: - Gun Guide shows your current gun bindings for five seconds, then collapses to a small icon with its configurable shortcut.

gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.kitchen.title: Mess Hall
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.kitchen.body: Craft a Mess Hall Mk I and a Cook Pot, then place both inside the beacon zone. Right-click the hall and insert at least two ingredients. Sandwich makes portable rations; Stew stocks a selected nearby empty pot. Bring a normal bowl and use a filled pot to eat a communal serving. Your empty bowl is reusable.
gui.arsenal_beacon.guide.kitchen.detail:
Sandwiches use one staple and one or two fillings, with 1–2 effects. Stew supports up to 3 effects and needs two different ingredient types. Mk I–IV batches consume 4/7/10/12 food items to make 4/8/12/16 servings. More items fund the batch; only different ingredients score effects. Split stacks do not improve strength. Containers return to the cook.

Chicken, mutton, rabbit and eggs add health; vegetables and milk add armor; mushrooms add knockback resistance; cooked fish and sweets add movement speed. Beef gives Firepower (gun damage); honey gives Quick Hands (reload speed); pork gives Brawler (gun bash damage); golden carrot gives Heavy Hand (gun bash knockback); pufferfish gives Demolition (grenade/rocket radius).

Meals last 30 minutes of field time. Inside a valid beacon zone their strength doubles and the timer freezes; returning home freezes the remaining time without refreshing it. Logout pauses the timer; dimension travel preserves it; death clears the meal. New meals replace old ones. Pot links reach 8 blocks. Mk I–IV support 1/2/3/4 pots. Upgrade through the hall menu; stored food and links are retained.
Mess Hall upgrades cost 8, 16 and 32 Reinforced Plating.
Mess Hall upgrades cost 4, 8 and 14 Ardent Energy.
